_**User (2026-02-06 21:05Z)**_

sometimes when Alfred is in front of a hotspot, hovering the mouse over alfred will show the alfred icon (to use stuff with him), sometimes it will show the interaction icon for the hotspot below. I'd like to know how the game determines precedence in hotspots, exits and sprites vs Aflred.

check ghidra to verify this

I've found the answer by examining the `check_mouse_on_sprites_and_hotspots` function in Ghidra:

**Why hovering over Alfred shows different icons:**

Alfred (sprite 1) is treated **specially** in the priority system:

1. When Alfred is detected, `mouse_hover_state = 0x03` is set, but the check **continues** (doesn't break)
2. The game then checks hotspots **only if** `mouse_hover_state` is `0x00` (nothing) **OR** `0x03` (Alfred)
3. If a hotspot is found at that position, it **overrides** Alfred with `mouse_hover_state = 0x02`

**Result:**
- **Alfred icon**: When Alfred is there but no hotspot overlaps
- **Hotspot icon**: When both Alfred AND a hotspot are at that position (hotspot wins)

**Other sprites** (non-Alfred) set `mouse_hover_state = 0x01` and **break immediately**, preventing any hotspot check - they always have priority.

This is intentional design: Alfred shouldn't block interactions with hotspots behind him, but other NPCs/objects do block hotspots.

I've documented the complete system in `MOUSE_PRIORITY_SYSTEM.md`.

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nCheck room 0 hotspots to see what's special about hotspots 1 and 5\nthat might cause them to be occluded by Alfred.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/ALFRED.1', 'rb') as f:\n    # Get room 0 pair 10 offset\n    f.seek(0x00)\n    room0_offsets = []\n    for i in range(13):\n        offset, size = struct.unpack('&lt;II', f.read(8))\n        room0_offsets.append((offset, size))\n    \n    pair10_offset = room0_offsets[10][0]\n    \n    # Read hotspot count\n    f.seek(pair10_offset + 0x47A)\n    hotspot_count = struct.unpack('&lt;H', f.read(2))[0]\n    \n    print(f\"Room 0 has {hotspot_count} hotspots\")\n    print()\n    \n    # Read all hotspots (9 bytes each at +0x47C)\n    f.seek(pair10_offset + 0x47C)\n    for i in range(hotspot_count):\n        flags = struct.unpack('&lt;B', f.read(1))[0]\n        x = struct.unpack('&lt;H', f.read(2))[0]\n        y = struct.unpack('&lt;H', f.read(2))[0]\n        w = struct.unpack('&lt;B', f.read(1))[0]\n        h = struct.unpack('&lt;B', f.read(1))[0]\n        extra = struct.unpack('&lt;H', f.read(2))[0]\n        \n        action_names = []\n        if flags &amp; 0x01: action_names.append(\"OPEN\")\n        if flags &amp; 0x02: action_names.append(\"CLOSE\")\n        if flags &amp; 0x04: action_names.append(\"PUSH\")\n        if flags &amp; 0x08: action_names.append(\"PULL\")\n        if flags &amp; 0x10: action_names.append(\"TALK\")\n        if flags &amp; 0x20: action_names.append(\"0x20\")\n        if flags &amp; 0x40: action_names.append(\"0x40\")\n        if flags &amp; 0x80: action_names.append(\"0x80_HIGH_BIT\")\n        \n        marker = \"\"\n        if i in (1, 5):\n            marker = \" &lt;--- USER REPORTED OCCLUDED BY ALFRED\"\n        \n        print(f\"Hotspot {i}: flags=0x{flags:02X} [{', '.join(action_names) if action_names else 'NONE'}]\")\n        print(f\"  Position: ({x}, {y}), Size: {w}x{h}, Extra: 0x{extra:04X}{marker}\")\n        if flags &amp; 0x80:\n            print(f\"  *** HAS BIT 0x80 SET - this might affect priority! ***\")\n        print()\n\nprint(\"\\n=== Analysis ===\")\nprint(\"The code does: uVar6 = CONCAT11(flags_byte, hotspot_index) &amp;   "textEditContent": "# Mouse Hover Priority System\n\n## Overview\nThe function &#96;check_mouse_on_sprites_and_hotspots&#96; @ 0x00019879 determines what icon/interaction is shown when hovering the mouse.\n\n## Confirmed Priority Rules (from assembly)\n\n### 1. Sprites (checked first, index 1 to sprite_count)\nFor each sprite, the function:\n1. Checks bounding box (x, y, w, h)\n2. Checks &#96;offset +0x21 != 0xFF&#96; (valid type) and &#96;offset +0x30 == 0x00&#96; (active)\n3. Checks **pixel transparency**: reads actual sprite pixel data at the mouse position — pixel must NOT be 0xFF (transparent)\n\nOn a pixel-level hit:\n- &#96;mouse_hover_state = 0x01&#96; (generic sprite)\n- If sprite index == 1 (Alfred): &#96;mouse_hover_state = 0x03&#96; instead\n- Stores &#96;hotspot_action_flags&#96;, &#96;hotspot_id_or_data&#96;, &#96;hotspot_sprite_index&#96;\n- **If NOT sprite 1**: &#96;break&#96; — exits sprite loop, skips hotspot check entirely\n- **If sprite 1 (Alfred)**: falls through — continues iterating remaining sprites\n\n### 2. Hotspots (checked second, conditionally)\nAfter the sprite loop, hotspots are checked **only if**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;asm\n00019b95: MOV CH,[0x00051755]    ; load mouse_hover_state\n00019b9b: TEST CH,CH              ; is it 0?\n00019b9d: JZ hotspot_loop         ; if 0 → check hotspots\n00019ba3: CMP EAX,0x3             ; is it 3 (Alfred)?\n00019ba6: JNZ skip_hotspots       ; if NOT 3 → skip hotspots\n; fall through to hotspot_loop\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSo hotspots are checked when &#96;mouse_hover_state == 0&#96; (nothing found) OR &#96;mouse_hover_state == 3&#96; (Alfred found).\n\nWhen a hotspot rectangle matches, the code **always** sets &#96;mouse_hover_state = 0x02&#96;, overriding Alfred:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;asm\n00019c48: MOV byte ptr [0x00051755],0x2   ; mouse_hover_state = 2 (ALWAYS)\n00019c4f: MOV DH,byte ptr [EAX + 0x47c]  ; load flags byte\n00019c55: AND DH,0x7f                      ; strip bit 7 (for storage only)\n00019c58: MOV byte ptr [0x00051757],DH    ; store as hotspot_action_flags\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nThe &#96;AND 0x7F&#96; only affects the **stored action flags** — it does NOT affect the hover state assignment. &#96;mouse_hover_state&#96; is unconditionally set to 2.\n\n### 3. Exits (always checked)\nExit detection is always checked at the end, regardless of sprite/hotspot results. ## Corrected Analysis

My previous 0x80 flag theory was completely wrong — I was reading the hotspot data with a 2-byte count instead of 1-byte, which produced garbage. The actual room 0 hotspots 1 and 5 both have `flags=0x00` (LOOK only).

**What the code actually does:**

The `AND DH,0x7F` at address `0x19c55` only strips bit 7 from the **stored action flags** — it does NOT affect detection. When a hotspot rectangle matches the mouse position, `mouse_hover_state` is **always** set to `0x02`, unconditionally overriding Alfred's `0x03`.

**So hotspots always win over Alfred in the detection code.** The only way Alfred can "occlude" a hotspot is **geometrically**: if Alfred's sprite extends beyond the hotspot rectangle, the mouse can be on Alfred's pixels but outside the hotspot rect. At those positions, only Alfred is detected (state 3, Alfred cursor). But anywhere the mouse is on BOTH Alfred AND within the hotspot rectangle, the hotspot will win (state 2, interaction cursor).

Could what you're observing be that Alfred is simply larger than those hotspot rects? Hotspot 1 (bed) is (123,146)-(223,195) and hotspot 5 (bookshelf) is (303,164)-(393,192) — if Alfred stands in front of them, parts of his sprite would extend above/below/around those relatively small rectangles, showing the Alfred cursor on those edge pixels.
